newsitem.title: NEPAL: Nepali women rally against fuel price hike.
newsitem.headline: Nepali women rally against fuel price hike.

text.p: About 800 Nepali housewives held a rally on Friday to protest against a government decision to raise fuel prices, organisers and witnesses said.
Housewives, carrying banners and placards, shouted slogans demanding that the three-month-old coalition government rescind last week's price hike.
The government has raised the price of petrol by 14.7 percent, diesel by 25 percent, kerosene by 15.7 percent and cooking gas by 60 percent.
"Bring down the prices of oil and gas," read one placard.
The move to raise prices has been criticised not only by the main opposition Nepali Congress party but also by members of the ruling coalition, including the communists, who dominate the alliance.
Nepali bus and truck owners on Monday said the increase in domestic oil prices came despite flat global crude prices, and threatened to raise fares unless the government withdrew the increase.

The state-owned Nepal Oil Corporation, which has a monopoly over the import and distribution of petroleum products in the Himalayan kingdom, imports some 600,000 tonnes of petroleum products every year.
It says imports are becoming more and more expensive and the price rise is essential to save the corporation from making a loss.
